newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Bodies of two Americans found at Cambodian crash site.
newsitem.headline: Bodies of two Americans found at Cambodian crash site.

text.p: Rescuers on Friday tried to recover the bodies of two Americans killed when their light aircraft crashed on Cambodia's highest mountain, government officials said.

"There are no survivors," said Defence Secretary of State Ek Sereywath, adding that a helicopter had managed to lower one man to the crash site around the 1,700 metre (5,600 feet) mark on Mount Oral on Friday morning and he had spotted the two bodies.

He said a helicopter had been sent to the mountain on Friday morning to try to recover the bodies of the two unidentified Americans, who went missing on Wednesday after setting out on a night time geological survey of the Tonle Sap (Great Lake) area.
The pilot and technician were working for the Japan National Oil Corporation, which is exploring for oil and gas reserves under the vast lake.
Air force officer You Vireak, a coordinator of the rescue operation, confirmed the two men had been killed.
A U.S. Embassy spokeswoman was unable to confirm the two men were dead, but an American diplomat told Reuters on Wednesday the chances they had survived were not good.
Witnesses said U.S. special forces had been involved in the search for the men and wreckage, which was first sighted on Wednesday in heavy jungle.
Ek Sereywath said the plane had crashed because of bad weather, which had hampered the search operation. "It was not engine trouble," he said.
